answer: Each epoch a miner files a hash of its answer with a private salt before the voyage window shuts. The three words arrive afterward from a public beacon, so no draft sees the prompt. At reveal the ledger rehashes, matches each word to the beacon, and checks the salt's 300 POA bond; an unopened hash forfeits it, duplicate text voids both. A stolen reveal is worthless, the window shut. A thousand blind drafts cost $600 of inference an epoch and 300,000 POA locked, and salts from one wallet still fold. A lotus rises from a garden pond it never chose; the root, not the surface, decides.
